headline: Low interaction risk: both open-source docs-only agents have no network egress or shared I/O surfaces, so pairwise harms are mostly absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented: both profiles show io_surfaces empty and network_egress none, so there is no plausible default path for one agent’s output to be injected into the other. The pair is open-source docs-only, but the interaction pathway is still absent in both profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not connect either agent to a shared clipboard or message queue.
Review any future orchestrator for provenance tagging.
requires-engineering: add explicit input sanitization if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, shared workspace, or outbound network egress, so there is no documented route for one agent to leak the other’s data. Because both are docs-only and unverified, I avoid assuming hidden storage or upload behavior.
conditions: IF either agent is later given access to sensitive files or a shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of both agents’ working directories.
Disable any future file-sync or export integration.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before enabling shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces are documented: both io_surfaces and concurrency_model are empty, and network egress is none for both. Without a shared mutable resource, there is no plausible write conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access.
Assign separate repositories or folders.
Avoid running both under the same mutable state.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error path is not documented, but mem0’s knowledge-management role could plausibly consume outputs from the data-engineering course if an operator wires them together. Because both profiles are docs-only and no default input chain is shown, this remains a low, configuration-dependent risk.
conditions: IF mem0 is configured to ingest outputs from the data-engineering agent without verification, erroneous content can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before mem0 stores any output.
Require source citations on imported content.
Limit mem0 ingestion to approved schemas.
Turn off automatic downstream actions on imported notes.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented in either profile. Since both agents are open-source docs-only and touch no declared regulated data, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to score.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data or a residency-bound deployment, compliance must be reassessed.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into either agent.
Document any future retention policy before deployment.
Separate EU and US data flows if added later.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review before production use.
